en-US.description:
Your computer's coding agent, from your phone.

Not a hosted copy of it — the actual agent process on your own machine, in your own repo, signed in with your own account, reached over your own private network.

A small open-source daemon runs on your Mac, Linux box or PC. This app is the client. You scan a QR code once, and from then on the work stays where it is while the keyboard moves.

WHAT YOU CAN DO

• Start a chat in any folder on your computer and watch the answer stream in, token by token.
• Approve before anything runs. In ask mode every shell command stops for your decision, and a dangerous one stops even when you have loosened the rules.
• Get a push when a command is waiting. Allow or deny it from the lock screen; nothing runs while you decide.
• Keep the turn alive. Close the app, lose signal, go into a tunnel — the turn keeps running on the computer and the phone catches up when it reconnects.
• Talk instead of typing. Record a voice message and your computer transcribes it.
• Attach a photo, a file or a screenshot to the conversation.
• Reach several computers, switch between projects, and pin, rename, archive or search your chats.
• See what a turn actually cost and how much of your usage window is left.

WHAT IT IS NOT

There is no account here, no server of ours, and no API key in the middle. Nothing you type is sent to the developer. The app talks to your own daemon directly, over your local network or your own private network.

WHAT YOU NEED

A computer running the free and open-source remote-ai-chat daemon — macOS, Linux or Windows — with a coding agent command-line tool already installed and signed in on it. Installation takes one command. Source code, setup instructions and the full wire protocol are public:

https://github.com/yakubilik/remote-ai-chat

Without that daemon this app has nothing to connect to.
en-US.promotionalText: Approve the command from the bus. The turn keeps running at home.
